about: Every state's and the District of Columbia's rule for a tied election, by kind of office, each read at the state's own code (or marked otherwise). A rule's quotation was verified word for word against the fetched text by pipeline/intake/state_law.py. Written 2026-11-07T07:52Z.

unread.reason: not fetched; outside the canvass, recount and tie chapters that were read

notes: Alaska's statute site (akleg.gov/basis/statutes.asp, print view by section range) answered with text for every page. elections.alaska.gov (the Division of Elections) was not used.

The earlier reader's lead for Alaska was confirmed for AS 15.20.530, 15.15.460 and 15.20.430-.450; the earlier note that any recount other than on a tie is on application stating a belief of mistake is also confirmed. New here: general elections are ranked-choice (AS 15.15.350), with a tie rule inside the count, and the open top-four primary has its own tie-for-fourth rule (AS 15.25.100).

rules.applies_to: an office for which only one candidate is to be elected, in a general election (U.S. Senate and House, governor and other statewide offices, state legislative seats)
rules.steps: if two or more candidates tie for the highest number of votes, the director notifies the tied candidates and immediately proceeds with the recount under AS 15.20.430-15.20.530; if after the recount and appeal two or more candidates still tie, the director notifies them of a time and place to determine the successful candidate by lot and certifies the result. A candidate for the state legislature or Congress who believes the recount erred may appeal to the chamber in which the candidate seeks membership (AS 15.20.520), and the legislature's power to judge its members is not limited (AS 15.20.560).
rules.who: the director of elections draws the lot

sources.quote: If two or more candidates tie in having the highest number of votes for the same office for which there is to be elected only one candidate, the director shall so notify the candidates who are tied. The director shall immediately proceed with the recount of votes in the manner provided by

If after a recount and appeal two or more candidates tie in having the highest number of votes for the same office, the director shall notify the candidates who are tied. The director shall notify the candidates of a reasonably suitable time and place to determine the successful candidate by lot.

in the event of a tie between the final two continuing candidates, the procedures in [...] shall apply to determine the winner of the general election; in the event of a tie between two candidates with the fewest votes, the tie shall be resolved by lot to determine which candidate is defeated.

rules.note: General elections are counted by ranked-choice voting (AS 15.15.350(c)); a tie between the final two continuing candidates goes to the same recount-then-lot procedure, and a tie for fewest votes in an earlier round is resolved by lot to decide who is defeated. AS 15.15.460 speaks of "the same office for which there is to be elected only one candidate"; all three kinds listed are single-winner offices in Alaska, which is [inferred] from the offices' nature, not stated in the section.

rules.who: the director of elections

sources.quote: Electors of President and Vice President of the United States are selected by election at the general election in presidential election years, in the manner and as determined by the ranked-choice method of tabulating votes described in
in the event of a tie between the final two continuing candidates, the procedures in [...] shall apply to determine the winner of the general election

rules.note: No section on a tie for presidential electors as such was found in AS 15.30.010-15.30.090. The reading is that AS 15.30.010 sends the count to AS 15.15.350, whose tie rule then applies. Electors are voted for through the presidential ticket (AS 15.30.050), so a tie would be a tie between tickets.

rules.applies_to: the open (top-four) primary: a tie between two candidates for the fourth greatest number of votes for an office
rules.steps: the primary follows the general-election provisions on the determination of tie votes and recounts; if two candidates tie for fourth place, the director decides which name goes on the general election ballot, by lot under AS 15.20.530 where the director cannot decide because the votes are equal
rules.who: the director of elections

sources.quote: If two candidates tie in having the fourth greatest number of votes for an office in the primary election, the director shall determine under (g) of this section which candidate's name shall appear on the general election ballot.
If the director is unable to make a determination under this section because the candidates received an equal number of votes, the determination may be made by lot under

Unless specifically provided otherwise, all provisions regarding the conduct of a general election shall govern the conduct of a primary election, including [...] provisions for the determination of tie votes and of recount, contests, and appeal

rules.note: The statute says the determination "may be made by lot"; that a recount comes first is [inferred] from AS 15.25.090 carrying the general-election tie and recount provisions to the primary, with AS 15.20.530 requiring the recount before the lot. Only a tie at the cut-off (fourth place) matters in the top-four primary; a tie for the highest vote in the primary does not decide who wins anything.

notes: Alabama is partly read: every rule recorded rests on the Alabama Law Institute's Election Handbook (20th edition), a state agency guide on the Legislature's own site, which is a lower grade than the statute; the quotations are the guide's words and each rule is marked stated. No compilation or other publisher was read for any Alabama section: Justia refused us (HTTP 403) when the amendment of 07:21 allowed trying it, and Cornell LII does not carry the Code of Alabama. Search results naming Justia, FindLaw and others were used only to learn the section numbers (17-12-23 and 17-13-21).

Handbook chapters read: 2, 8, 9, 11, 12, 18. Chapters 2, 8, 11 and 12 (elections generally, conduct of elections, Secretary of State, Judge of Probate) have no tie or recount rule beyond the second (runoff) primary when no one has a majority.

rules.applies_to: a tie in a general election (Code of Alabama 17-12-23, the section the search results name as "How tie vote decided")
rules.note: NOT READ: the Code section itself could not be read (see unread). The Law Institute handbook chapters read (2, 8, 9, 18) say nothing about a tie in a general election. A lead only, not recorded as a rule: the House-engrossed text of HB144 (2022 Regular Session, on the Legislature's site, strike-outs not visible in the extracted text) has a caption saying a tie between two candidates for a county or precinct office is decided by lot by the judge of probate, and its text for 17-12-23 puts senator, representative and state-officer ties to the Secretary of State to decide by lot in the Governor's presence; whether that became law and what the Code now says was not read.

rules.applies_to: a municipal election (a city or town council or commission office) in which the second or runoff election ends in a tie; state general law as summarised by the handbook, municipal charters not read
rules.steps: when no candidate has a majority, the municipal governing body orders a runoff between the top two; a tie is decided by a majority vote of the entire municipal governing body
rules.who: the municipal governing body

sources.quote: A tie is decided by a majority vote of the entire municipal governing body.

rules.note: From an agency guide that cites 11-46-55(d), not from the Code. The handbook predates 2022; HB144 (2022 Regular Session, engrossed text read) would add that if the governing body fails to break the tie the judge of probate decides by lot. Whether that is law now was not read. County and precinct offices: unread.

Surprise: a tie for the state executive offices other than the Commissioner of State Lands is decided by the two houses of the General Assembly voting jointly; ties for Congress, the legislature and the Commissioner of State Lands go to a special runoff four weeks after the election; county and municipal ties go to a runoff, then a lot.

The guide also says (not recorded as a rule): a tie for second place is settled by lot at the county board, and the order of candidates' names on the ballot is determined by lot at a commission meeting.

rules.applies_to: U.S. Senate and House in a general election; the guide's words speak of "the qualified electors of the congressional district"
rules.steps: the two tied candidates are placed on a special runoff ballot held four weeks after the general election, voted on by the qualified electors
rules.who: the voters, in a special runoff

sources.quote: If any two (2) candidates receiving the highest number of votes also receive an equal number of votes, a tie shall exist, and a special runoff election must be held four (4) weeks from the day of the general election with the names of those two (2) candidates placed on a special runoff election ballot to be voted upon by the qualified electors of the congressional district.

rules.note: From an agency guide that cites A.C.A. 7-5-703(c), not from the Code. The guide's wording is about the congressional district (the House); that the same section governs the U.S. Senate (statewide electors) is [inferred] and was not stated.

If no candidate received a majority of the votes cast for the office or if a tie vote exists, a runoff election is held in the district at the same time as the general election held in November.

notes: Arizona's own statute site (azleg.gov/ars) answered with text for every section. The earlier reader reported the Arizona election office refused; the legislature's site did not.

Surprise: in Delaware a tie in a general election is not settled by a lot at all in the sections read: the court certifies a vacancy, and a vacancy in the General Assembly or in the House is filled by a special election; a municipal tie is a new election run by the State Election Commissioner; a primary tie goes to the party's committee.
Delaware's automatic recount thresholds are the lesser of 1,000 votes and one-half of one percent of the two candidates' votes, which is mainly the percentage for any race under about 200,000 votes.

rules.applies_to: State Senator and State Representative in a general election
rules.steps: the court (the Superior Court sitting as the county board of canvass) certifies to the Governor that a vacancy will occur in the office; a vacancy in either house by reason of failure to elect is filled by a writ of election issued by the presiding officer within 10 days, and the special election is set 30 to 35 days after the writ (or at the general election if the vacancy falls in the stated window)
rules.who: the voters, in a special election; the presiding officer of the house issues the writ

sources.quote: If, by reason of an equal number of votes having been cast for 2 or more individuals for an office, it appears to the Court that a vacancy will occur in that office, the Court shall create a certificate of this fact, under its seal, and deliver this certificate to the Governor under § 5709 of this title.

Whenever there is a vacancy in either house of the General Assembly, by reason of failure to elect, ineligibility, death, resignation or otherwise, within 10 days of the creation of the vacancy a writ of election shall be issued by the presiding officer of the house in which the vacancy exists

the officer issuing the writ shall set the day for holding the special election for the vacancy in the General Assembly, but such day shall not be less than 30 nor more than 35 days next after the day of issuing the writ.

rules.note: Del. Code tit. 15, sections 5708, 7101 and 7102. The chain from a tie to a special election is read across two sections: 5708 makes a tie a vacancy, and 7101 lists "failure to elect" among the vacancies filled by writ of election. A recount at state expense comes first if the margin is under the threshold (section 5702(e)), which a tie always is, so recount-then-new-election in effect.

rules.applies_to: any primary, special primary, election or special election for public office in which no candidate receives a majority
rules.steps: no candidate is nominated or elected without a majority of the votes cast; where no candidate receives a majority, a run-off between the candidates with the two highest numbers of votes is held; the highest vote in the runoff wins (the bill text sets the runoff dates: the ninth week after a primary or a federal general election, the twenty-eighth day after other general elections)
rules.who: not stated in the text read

sources.quote: In instances where no candidate receives a majority of the [...] votes cast, a run-off primary, special primary runoff, run-off election, or special election [...] runoff between the candidates receiving the two highest numbers of votes shall be held.

In the case of a runoff from a general election for a federal office [...] or special election for a federal office held in conjunction with a general [...] election, the runoff shall be held on the Tuesday of the ninth week following such general [...] election.

In the case of a runoff from a general election for an office other than a federal office [...] or a runoff from a special primary or special election for an office other than a federal [...] office held in conjunction with a general election, the runoff shall be held on the [...] twenty-eighth day after the day of holding the preceding general or special primary or [...] general or special election.

rules.note: The text does not use the word 'tie' and does not say what happens when the two highest numbers are equal. A tied two-candidate contest leaves no candidate with a majority, so a runoff between the same two follows [inferred]; for more than two tied candidates, or a tie for second place, the text read gives no rule. Municipal charters may provide for election by plurality (subsection (b) of the same section), in which case this runoff does not apply to that municipality; charters were not read. The text is a bill, not the Code in force (see the section's note), so the rule is marked inferred and the Code should be read before any figure rests on it.

Louisiana has two systems at once since 2026: closed party primaries (with a second party primary) for Congress, the supreme court, BESE and the Public Service Commission, and the open primary followed by a general election for every other office. A tie rule is recorded for each.

Louisiana has no automatic recount and no margin-triggered recount in Title 18 as printed; a candidate (or, for a proposition, a voter) may ask for a recount of the absentee-by-mail and early-voting ballots only, at their own cost, when those ballots could change the result.

Massachusetts has no automatic recount in the sections read; recounts are on voters' petitions (ten voters in a ward or town, any margin; 1,000 voters statewide within one-half of one per cent; district-wide within one-half of one per cent).

rules.applies_to: a state primary (and a city or town primary under chapter 53) when the tie is for the last nomination(s) available
rules.steps: if the number of persons receiving equal votes exceeds the number of nominations available there is deemed to be a vacancy; for an office filled by all the voters of the commonwealth the state committee fills it, for any other office the members of the ward and town committees in the district fill it; the choice must be one of the candidates who received the tie vote
rules.who: the state committee (statewide offices) or the ward and town committees of the district (other offices) of the party

sources.quote: In case of a tie vote where the number of persons receiving equal votes exceeds the number of nominations available, there shall be deemed to be a vacancy.
All vacancies caused by ties shall be filled only by the choice of one of the candidates receiving the tie vote.

rules.note: M.G.L. c. 53, s. 53. Chapter 53 s. 85 and s. 81 (tie votes at caucuses) are about caucuses and were not treated as primaries.

notes: Maryland's Election Law article has no tie-break for a general election for Congress, the electors or the legislature; ties are in the Constitution (Governor and Lieutenant Governor by the General Assembly with a lot as the last step; Attorney General by the Governor; Delegates and Senators by the party central committee and the Governor; other officers by a new election ordered by the Governor) and in a few Election Law sections (primary for a one-county office by the party central committee; boards of education).
Maryland has no automatic recount: every recount is on the petition of a candidate (or, for a question, of a registered voter) at a margin of 5% or less, free at 0.25% or less.

notes: Maine settles every tie by first recounting (automatic), then by a different method for each kind of office: lot for a primary, a special election for county offices and the legislature, the Legislature in joint ballot for presidential electors and for Governor (Constitution), the negative vote for a referendum.

Maine uses ranked-choice voting in primaries and in federal general elections (21-A 723-A); a tie between last-place candidates in an earlier round is decided by lot at once and is not a tie for the office.

rules.applies_to: a primary election, for any office
rules.steps: when there is an apparent tie the Secretary of State automatically initiates a recount; if the recount confirms the tie, the Secretary of State notifies the tied persons to be present at the office and selects the nominee publicly by lot; in a ranked-choice primary a tie for the most votes in the final round is decided the same way
rules.who: the Secretary of State

sources.quote: When there is an apparent tie vote, the Secretary of State shall automatically initiate a recount. If a recount confirms a tie vote, the following provisions apply.

In a primary election, the Secretary of State shall notify each person involved in the tie to be present at the Secretary of State's office at a certain time. At that time, the Secretary of State shall select the nominee publicly by lot.
A tie between candidates for the most votes in the final round must be decided as provided in section 732

rules.note: 21-A M.R.S. 732(1) and 723-A(3). A tie between last-place candidates in an earlier ranked-choice round is a different thing: it is decided by lot at once (723-A(3)) and is not a tie for the nomination.

Minnesota's recounts are all on a written request (there is no automatic recount of a candidate race); the publicly funded ones are free to the candidate within the thresholds, and a constitutional amendment within one-quarter percent is recounted without a request.

notes: All sections were read one at a time at the Revisor of Statutes' site (revisor.mo.gov); no refusal. One fetch of a section number that does not exist (115.602, tried as a neighbour of 115.601) returned the site's own page 'Trying to access pages that don't exist will be directed here' with the line 'Speeding: 0'; it was not a refusal, no further numbers were guessed, and the sections after it were taken from the chapter's table of contents.

Missouri has no recount without a request, a contest or a petition by the election authority. The one margin rule is RSMo 115.601: one-half of one percent for those who filed with the secretary of state, to be requested within seven days after certification; one percent for a contestant whose contest is heard by a court. Section 115.575(1) nonetheless calls the 115.601 recount 'automatic'.

A tie is settled by a special election among the tied candidates only (the governor orders it for federal and state legislative offices, the officer with whom they filed for the rest), or by the general assembly for the six state officers and for electors, or by lot if every tied candidate agrees.

rules.applies_to: governor, lieutenant governor, secretary of state, state auditor, state treasurer or attorney general, in a general election
rules.steps: the secretary of state issues a proclamation stating the tie; the general assembly, by joint vote and without delay at its next regular session, chooses one of the tied persons; the speaker of the house files a certificate with the secretary of state declaring who is elected
rules.who: the general assembly, by joint vote of both houses

sources.quote: If two or more persons receive an equal number of votes for election to the office of governor, lieutenant governor, secretary of state, state auditor, state treasurer or attorney general, and a higher number of votes than any other candidate for the same office, the secretary of state shall, immediately after the results of the election have been announced, issue a proclamation stating the fact, and the general assembly shall, by joint vote and without delay at its next regular session, choose one of such persons for the office.
The speaker of the house shall file a certificate declaring which person has been elected to the office with the secretary of state.

rules.note: RSMo 115.517.1. Subsection 4 (next rules) lets the tied candidates agree to a drawing of lots instead. The Missouri Constitution was not read for its own words on the governor.

The Secretary of State's 2026 county handbook (rev. 12/24/2025) repeats the county tie rule unchanged, which is some evidence that the 2017 text of 23-15-601 still holds.

Mississippi has no recount in the Election Code as printed: no automatic recount, no recount on request. A candidate may examine the ballot boxes (23-15-911) and may bring an election contest within twenty days (23-15-921, 23-15-951) or thirty days for a legislative seat (23-15-955). The straw draw is unusual: since 2017 a tie for a district office, a seat on the Supreme Court or Court of Appeals is decided by drawing straws from an opaque bag, not by lot or coin.
The governor's tie rule, changed in 2020, is the main thing not read.

notes: Every section was read one at a time on the Legislature's MCA site (mca.legmt.gov, 'Montana Code Annotated 2025'); no refusal. The index pages (chapter and part tables of contents) were read to find sections and are not cited.

Montana's tie rules are the most varied of the nine: after a recount, a tie for Congress goes to a special election ordered by the governor; for a supreme court justice, district judge or legislator the governor appoints one of the tied; for statewide executive officers the legislature elects by joint ballot; county commissioner, other county and subdivision offices are filled by appointment of one of the tied; a primary tie is decided by lot. Every certified tie is recounted first.

Recounts are all on petition except the tie recount: a free recount at one-quarter of one percent (or 10 votes for local offices, whichever is greater), a recount at one-quarter to one-half of one percent if the candidate posts a bond, and a court-ordered recount on probable cause at any margin.

rules.applies_to: nomination in a primary election
rules.steps: a certified tie first brings a recount as if a petition had been filed (13-16-203); if the recount still shows a tie and it cannot be determined who is nominated, the election officer with whom the candidates' nominating declarations or petitions were filed determines by lot which candidate is nominated, after written notice of the time and place of the drawing to each candidate
rules.who: the election officer with whom the candidates' nominating declarations or petitions were filed

sources.quote: If the recount shows a tie vote for any office and it cannot be determined who has been nominated by the primary election, the election officer with whom the candidates' nominating declarations or petitions were filed shall determine by lot which candidate shall be nominated. Written notice of the time and place of the drawing shall be given to each candidate involved.
the administrator or the secretary of state shall proceed as if a petition for a recount has been filed. If a tie exists after the recount, the tie must be resolved as provided by law.

rules.note: MCA 13-16-501(1) and 13-16-203(1). 13-15-405(1) excepts 13-10-204 (primary results), which was not read.

notes: Nebraska settles a tie only after a recount: 32-1122 begins "If a recount ... results in" a tie. 32-1038(2) gives the board of state canvassers a lot with no recount condition, so both are cited. Executive-department offices (governor, secretary of state, auditor, treasurer, attorney general) go to the Legislature, not to a lot.
Nebraska's automatic recount margin is measured against the winning candidate's votes, not the total votes cast, and is one percent (two percent where 500 or fewer votes were cast).

rules.applies_to: persons "returned with an equal and the highest number of votes" at the state canvass, for offices other than the executive branch
rules.steps: the board of state canvassers (Governor, Secretary of State, Auditor, Treasurer, Attorney General) decides by lot which of the tied persons is elected; where a recount is held (section 32-1119) and still leaves a tie, section 32-1122(5) gives the same lot

sources.quote: If any two or more persons are returned with an equal and the highest number of votes, the board of state canvassers shall decide by lot which of such persons is elected except for officers elected to the executive branch.

If a recount after a general or special election results in any two or more persons having an equal and the highest number of votes for an office canvassed by the board of state canvassers, the board shall decide by lot which of such persons is elected, except officers elected to the executive department.

rules.note: The text does not name U.S. Senate, U.S. House, presidential electors or the Legislature. Ohio sends a tie for governor and the four other executive offices to the general assembly, not to a lot; the statewide lot in 3505.35(A) applies to every other statewide election and, for the five executive offices, is only a preliminary declaration.

rules.applies_to: the offices of governor and lieutenant governor (as joint candidates), secretary of state, auditor of state, treasurer of state and attorney general, at a regular state election (section 3505.34)
rules.steps: the president of the senate canvasses the abstracts before a majority of the members of each house of the general assembly in the first week of the regular session after the election; if two or more candidates (or sets of joint candidates for governor and lieutenant governor) receive the largest and an equal number of votes, one of them is declared elected by a majority of the votes of all the members of the senate and the house of representatives
rules.who: the general assembly (senate and house voting together)

sources.quote: If two or more candidates for election to the same office, or two or more sets of joint candidates for governor and lieutenant governor, receive the largest and an equal number of votes, one of them, or one set of joint candidates for governor and lieutenant governor, shall be declared elected to such office by a majority of the votes of all of the members of the senate and the house of representatives of the general assembly.

rules.note: Section 3505.35(A) also says a tie in a statewide election is resolved by lot by the secretary of state and names joint candidates for governor, but it adds that the secretary of state's declaration, for these five offices, is only for fixing the time of the commencement of the recount-application period (it quotes section 3515.02); so the general assembly's canvass is read as the one that decides these five offices [inferred]. The Ohio Constitution was not read.

notes: Title 26 was read as one PDF (the legislature's documented download); the whole title was searched for the words tie, tied, by lot, recount and automatic, and chapter 8 (sections 26-8-101 to 26-8-122) was read in full.

Oklahoma recounts of candidate races have no margin condition and are at the petitioner's cost, so a recount does not by itself follow a close margin; there is no automatic recount for candidate races.

A tie is settled by lot at the election board's public meeting, except: a primary tie for first place among three or more candidates where a runoff primary is to be held (the tied names go on the runoff ballot), and elections of elective state officers, where the Constitution (Art. VI, section 5) has the Legislature choose by joint ballot.

rules.applies_to: the nomination or election of "any candidate" in any Runoff Primary, General Election or Primary Election, except elections of state officers under Section 5 of Article VI of the Oklahoma Constitution (see the separate rule); for county offices the county election board, for offices filed with the State Election Board that board
rules.steps: when a tie vote is certified, the election board authorized to issue the certified list or certificate of election selects the nominee or electee by lot at a public meeting, in the presence of the candidates or their designees; the secretary notifies the tied candidates in writing by registered or certified mail at least five days before; the names are written on equal pieces of paper, put in opaque containers, tumbled in a transparent container, and a person other than the candidates draws one; if the tie appears at a recount, the board selects by lot at the meeting called for the recount or the issuing of the certificate
rules.who: the county election board, or the State Election Board for offices whose declarations of candidacy it accepts

sources.quote: When a tie vote is certified in the nomination or election of any candidate in any Runoff Primary, General Election, or Primary Election, the election board that is authorized by law to issue the certified list or certificate of election shall, at a public meeting of the board and in the presence of the candidates involved or their designee, if they or any of them desire to be present, select the nominee or electee by lot.

In the event of a tie involving candidates, the election board authorized by law to issue the certified list or certificate of election shall, at the meeting called to conduct the recount or to issue the certified list or certificate of election, in the presence of the candidates involved, if they or any of them desire to be present, select the nominee or electee by lot substantially as prescribed in paragraphs 3 and 4 of Section 8-105 of this title.

rules.note: The text says "any candidate" in a Primary, Runoff Primary or General Election and does not name federal, state or local offices; reading it as covering U.S. Senate and House, legislative and local offices is an inference. A tie does not lead to a new election: section 26-8-122 (new election ordered by the governor when no winner can be determined after a hearing) says it does not apply to elections resulting in tie votes, which are determined as provided by law. No recount is required before the lot; the second source says the lot is drawn at the recount meeting if a tie is found there.

South Dakota recounts a tie automatically and then, if still tied, draws lots (state and county offices); in municipal and school elections a tie goes to lots after an optional recount.

rules.applies_to: a tie vote found on the canvass of the original official returns for an office or position, in an election covered by chapter 12-21 (not school, township or municipal elections, which have their own sections) (SDCL 12-21-16 and 12-21-43)
rules.steps: the canvassing board certifies the tied vote to the county auditor (election confined to a county) or to the secretary of state (all other elections); that officer proceeds as if a petition for a recount of all votes involved had been filed, and the recount is made; if a tie is found on the recount and it cannot be determined who is nominated or elected, the authority charged with issuing the certificate fixes a time and place and the candidates draw lots, in person or by representative, and the certificate is issued accordingly
rules.who: the county auditor or the secretary of state (recount); the authority charged by law with issuing the certificate of election or nomination (lot)

sources.quote: Whenever by reason of a tie vote found to exist upon the canvass of the original official returns, it is impossible to declare who has been elected or nominated to an office or position, it shall thereupon be the duty of the official board making such canvass to certify said vote to the county auditor where the election involved is confined to or within the limits of a county, and to the secretary of state as to all other elections.

Thereupon such county auditor or such secretary of state, as the case may be, shall proceed exactly as if a petition had been duly filed under §§ 12-21-7 to 12-21-15, inclusive, requiring a recount to be made of all votes [...] involved, and such recount shall proceed accordingly.

When a tie vote between candidates is found to exist on the basis of any such recount, and by reason of such tie vote it cannot be determined who has been nominated or elected, it shall be the duty of the authority charged by law with the responsibility of issuing the certificate of election or nomination to fix a time and place for the drawing of lots by such candidates involved in such tie vote

rules.note: The text says 'an office or position' and 'nominated or elected' and names no kind of office; the kinds are a mapping [inferred]. Presidential electors are covered by the same words and by the recount in 12-21-15 [inferred]. Whether the South Dakota Constitution gives the Legislature a role for a tie for governor or in judging its members' elections was not read (the Secretary of State's book reprints only some constitutional provisions and none on this was found). Township elections were not read. Under 12-21-18 chapter 12-21 does not apply to an election that must be followed by a runoff for want of a majority.

rules.applies_to: a race in which two or more candidates for an office receive an equal and the highest number of votes (a general or other election; for a primary see the next rule); excludes a race run by instant runoff voting under the Municipal Alternate Voting Methods Pilot Project
rules.steps: (1) the election officer must conduct a recount of the race, no later than 10 calendar days after the board of canvassers certifies the vote totals (20A-4-401(2)(a), (5)(a)(i)); (2) if the recount still leaves a tie, the board of canvassers declares a 'tie vote' (20A-4-304(1)(b)); (3) the election officer determines the winning candidate by lot, in whatever manner the officer determines, in a public meeting held no later than the first business day that is at least three calendar days after the recount canvass is completed, with notice to each tied candidate and a chance to watch the drawing or send a representative (20A-1-304(2))
rules.who: the election officer (county clerk, municipal clerk, special district clerk, or the lieutenant governor for a statewide or multi-county race)

sources.quote: The election officer shall conduct a recount of votes cast in a race if: (a) two or more candidates for an office receive an equal and the highest number of votes for that office

if, after conducting a recount under Subsection 20A-4-401(5), a tie vote occurs, the election officer shall, in a public meeting held no later than the first business day that is at least three calendar days after the day on which the recount canvass is completed: (a) determine the winning candidate, by lot, in whatever manner the election officer determines

rules.note: The words are 'a race' and 'an office' without limit; 20A-4-401(4) and (6) name statewide, multi-county, county, municipal and special district races, so those are explicit. Federal and state legislative offices are not named separately and are read within 'an office' [inferred]. A tie in an at-large race (several seats) is handled by 20A-4-401(2)(b) and (5)(b)(iv)(D): a tie vote is declared only if a lot is needed to fill the last seat. Municipal charters and special-district law were not read.

rules.applies_to: a tie in a primary election race, after the recount
rules.steps: the recount required by 20A-4-401(2) comes first; then the lot is cast by whoever the statute names for the office: for a national, statewide or other office that represents more than one county, the governor, lieutenant governor and attorney general at a public meeting called by the governor; for a county office, the district court judges of the district; any other primary (for example a municipal primary) the election officer under 20A-1-304(2). Each meeting is held no later than the first business day at least three calendar days after the recount canvass, with notice and a chance for each tied candidate to observe
rules.who: the governor, lieutenant governor and attorney general (national, statewide or multi-county office); the district court judges (county office); otherwise the election officer

sources.quote: a tie vote occurs in a primary election race for a national, statewide, or other office that represents more than one county, the governor, lieutenant governor, and attorney general shall, at a public meeting called by the governor [...] determine the winning nominee, by lot, in whatever manner the governor determines
a tie vote occurs in a primary election race for a county office, the district court judges of the district in which the county is located shall, at a public meeting called by the judges

rules.note: 20A-1-304(2) begins 'Except as provided in Subsection (3)', so subsection (3) displaces the election officer for these two classes of primary. A state legislative primary in a single county is not named in (3); it falls to subsection (2) or, if the district spans counties, to (3)(a) as 'other office that represents more than one county' [inferred].

VA.name: Virginia

code.name: Code of Virginia, Title 24.2 (Elections), and Constitution of Virginia, Article V
code.edition: the current Code as Virginia Law (the General Assembly's LIS site) prints it, pages dated 11/7/2026; 24.2-802.1 shows amendment by 2026, c. 1078

notes: Read in full from the site's chapter pages: Title 24.2 Chapter 6 (24.2-670 to 24.2-687), Chapter 8 (recounts and contests), Chapter 5 (nominations); and Article V sections 2, 13 and 15 of the Constitution of Virginia. Election contest sections of Chapter 8 (24.2-803 to 24.2-814) were read only for a tie sentence (24.2-803(H)).

There is no automatic recount in the sections read: every recount follows a defeated candidate's (or 50 voters') petition. Tie before a recount: lot (local, General Assembly, Congress, electors) or the General Assembly (Governor, with the Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General by cross-reference). Tie after a recount: a special election, except for Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General and electors.
Earlier lead 'VA lot (24.2-674)' is right for local, legislative, congressional and elector offices but does not cover the three statewide executive offices.

rules.applies_to: a county, city, town or district office where, before any recount, two or more persons have an equal and the highest number of votes
rules.steps: (1) the electoral board determines publicly by lot which of the tied candidates is declared elected (24.2-674); (2) a person who loses the lot may petition for a recount under Article 1 of Chapter 8 (24.2-674, last paragraph); (3) if that recount finds each party to the recount with an equal number of votes, the court issues a writ ordering a special election to decide the office (24.2-802.2(H))
rules.who: the local electoral board (the lot); the recount court (the later special election)

sources.quote: If, prior to a recount, two or more persons have an equal number of votes for any county, city, town, or district office, and a higher number than any other person, the electoral board shall proceed publicly to determine by lot which of the candidates shall be declared elected.
Any person who loses the determination by lot may petition for a recount pursuant to Article 1

Except in the case of a recount of an election for Governor, Lieutenant Governor, or Attorney General, or for elector of President or Vice President of the United States, if the court finds that each party to the recount has received an equal number of votes, it shall issue a writ promptly ordering a special election be held to determine which candidate is elected to the office.

rules.note: State general law only; town and city charters were not read. 'District office' is read to include school board and other district-wide local offices [inferred].

code.name: Vermont Statutes Annotated, Title 17 (Elections)
code.edition: Vermont Laws, the General Assembly's statutes site, 2025-2026 session (it shows amendments effective as late as April 30, 2026)

unread.what: who pays a local recount (chapter 55) and a statewide public question recount
unread.reason: not found in sections 2683 to 2688 and subchapter 9 of chapter 51; not a refusal

notes: Read in full as printed: 17 V.S.A. chapter 51 (conduct of elections, including subchapter 9 recounts), chapter 49 (nominations, primary section 2369) and chapter 55 (local elections). The three chapter pages are the General Assembly's own full-text pages.

Vermont's rule is a recount by right to a losing candidate at 2 percent (5 for State Representative and local office); the State pays the recounts under chapter 51 subchapter 9; a tie leads to a recount and then a runoff election, except in a primary (party committee) and for a public question (certified not passed).

rules.applies_to: a tie vote in a general or special election for a State or national office, county office, State Senator or State Representative (the canvassing committees of section 2592(a) to (d))
rules.steps: (1) the canvassing committee must at once petition the Superior Court for a recount (2592(l)(1)); (2) either tied candidate may instead notify the court that he or she is withdrawing, and the court then certifies the other candidate as winner (2592(l)(2)); (3) if the recount of a general election results in a tie, the court orders a runoff election within three weeks of the recount, on a date the court sets, with only the tied candidates on the ballot (2602k(a)(3), (b)); the statute's own word is 'runoff election' but it is a fresh election between the tied candidates, not a second round after a first with a majority rule
rules.who: the canvassing committee petitions; the Superior Court (Civil Division, Washington County, for State and congressional offices) recounts and orders the runoff

sources.quote: In the case of a tie vote, the canvassing committee shall forthwith petition the appropriate Superior Court for a recount pursuant to section 2602 of this title.
either of the candidates that is involved in a tie may notify the appropriate Superior Court that he or she is withdrawing, in which case the court shall certify the other candidate as the winner.

If a recount of a general election results in a tie, the provisions of this section shall apply, and the court shall order a runoff election to be held, within three weeks of the recount, on a date set by the court.

rules.note: Section 2592(l) says 'a tie vote' without limiting the office; the canvassing committees it works through are listed in 2592(a) to (d) for State and national offices, county offices, State Senator and State Representative, so those kinds are explicit. 'Federal' is read from 'national offices' in 2592(a) [inferred].

rules.steps: the choice among those tied is made, on five days' notice and not later than 10 days after the primary, by a meeting of the party's committee, which nominates one of the tied candidates; the committee is the State committee for a State or congressional office, the senatorial district committee for State Senate, the county committee for a county office, the representative district committee for State Representative; the chair certifies the nomination to the Secretary of State within 48 hours

code.edition: the Washington State Legislature's RCW site (app.leg.wa.gov) as it prints the chapters now; each section shows its own amendment history (29A.60.221: 2004 c 271 s 176; 29A.64.021: 2013 c 11 s 66; 29A.64.081: 2020 c 337 s 5)

notes: Read in full: RCW chapter 29A.60 and chapter 29A.64 (the site's full-chapter pages) and Article III s 4 of the State Constitution. Not read: chapter 29A.72 (initiatives and referenda), 29A.56 (presidential electors), the Washington Administrative Code on recounts.

Earlier lead 'WA lot, RCW 29A.60.221' is right for the offices that section names; it does not cover the statewide executive offices, which the Constitution (Art. III s 4) sends to a joint vote of the legislature. Earlier lead for recounts (2,000 votes and 0.5%; manual tiers 1,000 or 150 votes and 0.25%) is confirmed.

rules.applies_to: any federal, state, county, city, district or precinct office where two or more persons have an equal and highest number of votes for one and the same office
rules.steps: the official empowered to issue the original certificate of election gives notice to the tied persons to attend at the appropriate office at the time appointed, and there publicly decides by lot which is declared duly elected, and delivers the certificate to that person; separately, a difference of zero votes is less than 2,000 votes and less than one-half of one percent, so the mandatory recount of RCW 29A.64.021 also applies (no cost of it may be charged to a candidate)
rules.who: the official empowered by state law to issue the original certificate of election (the county canvassing board for local offices; the Secretary of State for offices whose declaration of candidacy was filed with the Secretary of State)

sources.quote: If the requisite number of any federal, state, county, city, district, or precinct officers have not been elected by reason of two or more persons having an equal and highest number of votes for one and the same office, the official empowered by state law to issue the original certificate of election shall give notice to the several persons so having the highest and equal number of votes to attend at the appropriate office at the time to be appointed by that official, who shall then and there proceed publicly to decide by lot which of those persons will be declared duly elected

notes: Read in full: W. Va. Code 3-6-9, 3-6-10, 3-6-12, 3-6-1, 3-5-17, and the article 5 and 6 section lists. 3-5-15 (primary results) was searched for a tie rule and holds none.

West Virginia's tie rule is the only one among my states with neither a lot nor a new election: the canvassing board, or the Governor after thirty days on a tied person's application, simply selects one of the tied persons. Its recount is a candidate's demand with no margin condition, at the candidate's cost unless the result changes.

rules.applies_to: any election in which two or more persons voted for the same office receive the highest and equal number of votes, so that the election is not decided by the returns
rules.steps: the Governor or the county board of canvassers, whichever is to declare the result, decides the tie 'by the election of one of such persons'; if the county board has not decided the tie within thirty days after finding it, any one of the tied persons may apply to the Governor, who breaks the tie by selecting one of them, certifies his choice to the board of canvassers and declares that person duly elected. No lot, no recount first and no new election is mentioned: the choice is the declaring body's (or the Governor's) own selection
rules.who: the board of canvassers of the county (the county commissioners), or the Governor where he is to declare the result or on a tied person's application after thirty days

sources.quote: Whenever the Governor or the board of canvassers of a county is to declare the result of an election, and it appears to him or them that two or more of the persons voted for have received the highest and equal number of votes for the same office, so that the election to the office is not decided by the returns, he, or they, being required to declare the result, shall decide the tie by the election of one of such persons

upon application to the Governor by any one of such persons so voted for, he shall break the tie by the selection of one of such persons and shall certify his choice to such board of canvassers and declare such person duly elected for the office for which such person was a candidate.

rules.note: The section says 'an election' and 'the same office' without limiting the office, so all offices are read to be covered; which offices the Governor himself declares (rather than the county boards) is not stated in this section and was not traced through other sections [inferred]. The selection is by a person or board, not by a chance device, so it is recorded as 'other', not 'lot'. Municipal charters were not read.

Wyoming settles every tie by lot (county canvassing board or the state canvassing board of governor, secretary of state, auditor and treasurer), and recounts automatically at under 1% of the lowest winning candidate's votes.

rules.applies_to: an office in the state abstract: state officers, justice of the supreme court, United States senator, representative in congress, district court and circuit court judges, members of the state legislature
rules.steps: the state canvassing board resolves a tie vote for an office in the state abstract at an open meeting by lots cast; for members of the state legislature, 22-16-105 sends the tie to this same rule
rules.who: the state canvassing board (governor, secretary of state, state auditor and state treasurer)

sources.quote: A tie vote for an office contained in the state abstract shall be resolved at an open meeting by lots cast by the state canvassing board.
The state canvassing board is the governor, secretary of state, state auditor and state treasurer.

the secretary of state shall tabulate a statewide abstract by counties of votes for president and vice-president, state officers, justice of the supreme court, United States senator, representative in congress, district court judges, circuit court judges, members of the state legislature and the votes for and against ballot propositions voted on by electors of a district larger than a county.

A tie vote shall be decided at an open meeting by lots cast by the county canvassing board or other authority holding the election, except in elections for members of the state legislature, which shall be determined as provided in W.S. 22-16-119.

rules.note: Which offices the state abstract holds comes from 22-16-116 (quoted). Whether a recount under 22-16-109(b) (a margin under 1%, which a tie meets) comes before the lot is not stated in these sections [inferred possible]; the sections do not say a recount is required first, so the resolution is recorded as the lot the sections name.
